findings.title: Returned SQL condition is not always parenthesized and can compose incorrectly
findings.body: getAuthorizationConditions can return an OR predicate for org/team scope, and getBaseConditions returns that auth condition unwrapped when there are no filters. If a caller adds more predicates, e.g. `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND startTime > x`, SQL operator precedence makes the extra predicate apply only to one side of the OR, potentially returning rows that should be filtered out. The service should return a fully parenthesized predicate, or wrap the final result in getBaseConditions, so the fragment is safe to embed alongside other conditions.

findings.title: Public options type makes teamId optional for team scope
findings.body: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions makes `teamId` optional for every scope, and the constructor accepts this loose type. TypeScript callers can pass `{ scope: 'team', userId, orgId }` without `teamId`; Zod validation then fails, `options` becomes null, and all queries silently use `1=0`. The previous discriminated union type would have caught the missing `teamId` at compile time. Use a discriminated public type or surface validation errors.

findings.title: Org scope skips org memberships when org has no child teams
findings.body: In buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, `userIdsFromOrg` is only fetched when `teamsFromOrg.length > 0`, even though `teamIds` already includes the org id. For an organization with no child teams, org memberships are never loaded, so the generated condition only matches team bookings and excludes individual bookings for org members. Fetch memberships for `teamIds` regardless of whether child teams exist.

findings.title: Exact SQL equality assertions depend on unordered repository result order
findings.body: The org-scope test asserts exact Prisma.sql equality with arrays of team and user IDs in a specific order, but the service builds those arrays from repository queries without explicit ordering. The SQL semantics are unaffected by order, but the assertion can fail nondeterministically if rows are returned in a different order. Sort IDs in the service or compare normalized sets.

findings.title: Breaking service API change without caller migration in this PR
findings.body: The class removes the previous public `findMany` method and changes condition methods to return `Prisma.Sql` instead of Prisma where inputs. This is a breaking contract change for any existing caller of the service. If callers are expected to compose raw SQL now, they should be updated in this PR or the old API should be retained/deprecated.
